Summary: According to the Population Census, as of October 1, 2020, the population of Tokyo was 13,982,112. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government reported an overall population of Tokyo as about 14.27 million as of October 1, 2025. The Tokyo Statistical Yearbook 2020 figure for Tokyo prefecture was 14.05 million people. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government area had 14 million people as of 2020. The sources do not provide a definitive answer for the exact population figure for Tokyo in 2020.

Summary: As of October 1, 2025, the population of Tokyo-to was estimated to be 14.273 million, making it the most populous prefecture in Japan, accounting for 11.6% of the country's total population. The Tokyo metropolitan area, which includes Tokyo-to, Kanagawa-ken, Saitama-ken, and Chiba-ken, had a population of 36.986 million, representing about 30.1% of Japan's population. The total population of Japan as of October 1, 2025, was 123.05 million.

    https://www.tokyobureau.com/2026/japan-population-tokyo
    ## Tokyo’s share of Japan’s population

Japan had an official population of 123.802 million on October 1, 2024. That was 550,000 fewer people than a year earlier, a decline of 0.44% and the country’s fourteenth consecutive annual decrease. Tokyo-to was Japan’s most populous prefecture and held 11.5% of the national population, according to the Statistics Bureau of Japan’s 2024 population estimates.

In plain language, about one in nine people in Japan lived in Tokyo-to in 2024. NEWS HIGHLIGHTS

Preliminary Counts of the 2025 Population Census of Japan released

The Statistics Bureau of Japan released the Preliminary Counts of the 2025 Population Census of Japan on May 29, 2026.

The Population Census has been conducted every five years since 1920 and the 22nd Census was conducted in October 2025.

- Population of Japan

The total population of Japan as of October 1, 2025, was 123.05 million. Compared to 2020, the population of Japan decreased by 3.097 million (-2.5%), and the rate of decline accelerated.

- Population by prefecture

According to the population by prefecture in 2025, the population of Tokyo-to was largest (14.246 million). The population of the Tokyo metropolitan area, which consists of Tokyo-to, Kanagawa-ken, Saitama-ken and Chiba-ken, was 36.986 million, which accounts for about 30% (30.1%) of the population of Japan.

- Population by municipality

According to the population by municipality in 2025, the population decreased in 1,558 (90.6%) of the 1,719 municipalities in Japan.

- Households

The total number of households was 57.125 million, which increased by 1.294 million (2.3%) during the 2020-2025 period. The members per household was 2.15 and remained on a decline.

Hereafter, the release of the basic complete tabulation on population and households, results of the labour force status of population, industry and occupation of employed persons, place of work or schooling, internal migration and so on will follow in sequence.

Website: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/index.html

Conducting of 2026 Economic Census for Business Activity

The SBJ and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry are conducting the Economic Census for Business Activity with June 1, 2026 as the reference date. The Economic Census for Business Activity aims to clarify the business activities of establishments and enterprises in Japan on both a national and regional level by comprehensively capturing accounting items such as sales (revenue) and expenses across all industrial sectors at the same point in time. Moreover, this survey also provides information on the population for various statistical surveys on establishments and enterprises.

[Release Dates] The preliminary results will be released by the end of May 2027, and the detailed results will be released in sequence from September 2027.

Website: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/e-census/2026/index.html

The 3rd UK Statistical Delegation to Japan (May 2026)

The 3rd Statistical Delegation from the United Kingdom visited Japan from May 26 to 28, 2026. They discussed several topics with the SBJ officials on "Social surveys," "Enterprise survey support project," "AI coding" and "Population Census." The visit is based on the Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) between the United Kingdom Statistics Authority (UKSA) and SBJ, which was signed on May 17, 2023, to establish the basis for in depth cooperation between both sides in the area of official statistics.

Website: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/info/meetings/bilateral/uk202605.html

Population for Japan

[Total Population]

The total population was 123,802 thousand, a decrease of 550 thousand compared with the previous year. The rate of decrease was 0.44 percent. The total population decreased for the fourteenth year in a row.

The male population was 60,233 thousand, a decrease of 260 thousand (0.43 percent), while the female population was 63,569 thousand, a decrease of 290 thousand (0.45 percent).

The natural change of the male population was negative for the twentieth year in a row, and that of the female population was negative for the sixteenth year in a row.

The migration change of the Japanese population was negative for the first time in two years, and that of the foreign population was positive for the three years in a row.

[Population by Age Group]

The population under 15 years old was 13,830 thousand (11.2 percent of the total population).

The population aged 15 to 64 was 73,728 thousand (59.6 percent of the total population).

The population aged 65 years old and over was 36,243 thousand (29.3 percent of the total population).

Population by Prefecture

[Population]

The top five prefectures in population were Tokyo-to, Kanagawa-ken, Osaka-fu, Aichi-ken and Saitama-ken. These prefectures account for 37.9 percent of the total population.

Tokyo-to had the largest population in 2024 (11.5 percent of the total population).

[Rates of Population Change]

The population increased in Tokyo-to and Saitama-ken. Tokyo-to had the highest rate of increase in population.

The population decreased in 45 prefectures. Akita-ken had the highest rate of decrease in population.

The percentage of the population under 15 years old was the highest in Okinawa-ken and lowest in Akita-ken.

The percentage of the population aged 15 to 64 was the highest in Tokyo-to and lowest in Akita-ken.

The percentage of the population aged 65 years old and over was the highest in Akita-ken and lowest in Tokyo-to, and it increased in 44 prefectures.
